title: Faculty position at Binghamton State University
summary: From 1969-70 he has been part-time faculty, bringing jazz musicians for concerts and workshops.

venues.name: State University of New York at Binghamton

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: So you moved to Binghamton -- so after you and your wife got married, you moved to Binghamton in about 1969.
Yes, this is where I married her, in '69, right.
And so now, since you've been here, you've begun to work in a variety of different situations.
Oh, yes. I have been -- become a member of the faculty at the State University here at Binghamton.
When did you start working — ?
Oh, you got a job the year that you moved in?
And around '69 and '70, sure.
And you worked -- now what exactly do you do for the university?

Well, at the time -- this is a part-time situation, where it's not a steady thing. I'm just on the faculty and every once in a while, I have given concerts, you know, and what do you call them? Student affairs, like I played and brought in many, many names in jazz to the university and what have you, workshops and what have you.
So now do you teach workshops or are you like in a kind of a coordinating position, where you organize workshops in which you participate and the musicians you bring in?
Yeah.
Or do you give regular classes?
No, it's more or less musicians that I bring in on workshops and what have you.
So you kind of oversee kind of seminars of a sort.
Yeah, right.
And you choose the people and they come up and you have them perform and they give workshops for students.
That's right, sure.
And you've been doing that --
I've been doing it on and off, you know, not much, but --
For the last ten years.
Sure, sure.
